'''Zhong Wanxie''' ({{zh|s=钟万勰}}; 24 February 1934 – 12 November 2023), also known as '''Wan-Xie Zhong''', was a Chinese civil engineer and physicist. He was a professor at the [[Dalian University of Technology]] who specializes in [[computational mechanics]] and [[engineering mechanics]]. He pioneered computational mechanics in China and served as the founding Chairman of the Chinese Association for Computational Mechanics and an executive committee member of the International Association for Computational Mechanics. He was elected an academician of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] in 1993.

== Biography ==
Zhong Wanxie was born on 24 February 1934 in [[Shanghai]], [[Republic of China (1912–1949)|Republic of China]]. His father, [[Zhong Zhaolin]] (钟兆琳), was a distinguished professor of electrical engineering at [[Shanghai Jiao Tong University]]. After graduating from [[Tongji University]] in 1956, he entered the Institute of Mechanics of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] and studied under [[Qian Weichang]] and [[Hu Haichang]]. From 1958, he taught mechanics at the [[University of Science and Technology of China]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |url=http://www.hlhl.org.cn/news/findnews/showsub.asp?id=385 |script-title=zh:钟万勰 |trans-title=Zhong Wanxie |website=Ho Leung Ho Lee Foundation |access-date=6 February 2019 |language=zh |archive-date=9 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190209124458/http://www.hlhl.org.cn/news/findnews/showsub.asp?id=385 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 1962, on the recommendation of Hu Haichang, Zhong was transferred to the [[Dalian University of Technology]] (DUT) to work under [[Qian Lingxi]].<ref name=":0" /> Their collaboration soon bore fruit. They published two papers in ''Science in China'' and ''Acta Mechanica Sinica'', on the "general variational theory of limit analysis and plasticity". The research was used in [[submarine]] design and was awarded national prizes.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Zhang|first1=Hong-wu|last2=Lin|first2=Jia-Hao|date=July 2009|title=Mourn for the loss of Professor L. X. Qian|url=https://www.cimne.com/iacm/News/Expressions%2025.pdf|journal=IACM Expressions|issue=25|pages=41|archive-date=22 October 2018|access-date=6 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181022153219/http://www.cimne.com/iacm/News/Expressions%2025.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> He remained a professor at DUT for the rest of his career.<ref name=":0" />

In the early 1970s, Zhong pioneered [[computational mechanics]], the use of computer technology in mechanics, in China.<ref name=":0" /> He led a team of scientists, including [[Cheng Gengdong]], that designed engineering software using [[group theory]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.chinavitae.com/biography/Zhong_Wanxie/bio|title=Biography of Zhong Wanxie|website=China Vitae|access-date=6 February 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.hlhl.org.cn/english/showsub.asp?id=385|title=Zhong Wanxie|website=Ho Leung Ho Lee Foundation|access-date=6 February 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref> It was successfully used to design major projects such as the Shanghai TV Tower, the Liaoning Indoor Stadium, and the [[Shanghai Indoor Stadium]].<ref name=":0" />

In 1984, he was elected the first chairman of the newly established Chinese Association for Computational Mechanics (CACM). Two years later, he was elected an executive committee member of the International Association for Computational Mechanics (IACM).<ref name=":1" />

Zhong was elected an academician of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] in 1993.<ref name=":0" /> He was awarded the [[State Natural Science Award]] multiple times<ref name=":0" /> and the [[Ho Leung Ho Lee Prize]] in Mathematics and Mechanics.<ref name=":1" /> He was an honorary professor of the [[University of Hong Kong]] and the [[University of Wales]].<ref name=":1" />

Zhong died on 12 November 2023, at the age of 89.<ref>{{cite news |author1=Yang Yi ({{lang|zh|杨毅}}) |url=https://news.sciencenet.cn/htmlnews/2023/11/512153.shtm |script-title=zh:著名工程力学与计算力学专家钟万勰院士逝世 |work=sciencenet.cn |date=12 November 2023 |access-date=10 February 2024 |language=zh}}</ref>
